# montecarlo_salesforce_data_cloud_credentials (Resource)

Salesforce Data Cloud credentials are the connected app Monte Carlo signs in as for Salesforce Data Cloud connections to use, with its consumer secret or with a JWT signed by a private key. The consumer secret and the private key are never returned.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auth_mode` (String) How Monte Carlo signs in. `oauth_client_credentials` takes `consumer_secret`. `jwt_bearer` takes `username` and `private_key`. Both take `domain` and `consumer_key`.
- `consumer_key` (String) Consumer key of the connected app Monte Carlo signs in as.
- `domain` (String) My Domain host of your org, such as `acme.my.salesforce.com`.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `consumer_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Consumer secret of the connected app, for `oauth_client_credentials`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `consumer_secret_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `consumer_secret_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `dataspace` (String) The one data space a query connection runs in. Once set, it can be changed but not cleared. Sending it in an update, even unchanged, moves row count collection for that data space's tables to the query connections using these credentials.
- `dataspaces` (List of String) Data spaces Monte Carlo collects metadata from.
- `private_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) PEM private key whose certificate is on the connected app, for `jwt_bearer`. It must be an unencrypted RSA key. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `private_key_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `private_key_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `username` (String) Salesforce user the JWT signs in as, for `jwt_bearer`.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
